answer: Each identity opens one falcon desk and issues crystal notes backed by reserve in a vault. An auditor recomputes the reserve ratio from the crystal price index and ledger; under-backed or double-counted reserves burn a 70-credit bond. Notes expire on a nebula calendar date, so no reserve backs notes past expiry. The fee is 27 for the first desk and 27+11(k-1) for the k-th per funder, so the 1000th costs 11016 and 1000 fake desks cost 5,521,500 plus 70,000 in bonds. A rented-reserve ring fails: one entry cannot satisfy two auditors. An honest desk pays 27 and recovers its bond after clearance.
